reason: A court should sort the rescue quickly. I don't want a fight over who owns it, and my bills are already high.
The people who lent the money should lose it, not the bill payers. Customers and staff running it seems fair.
Bills have gone up for years while the bosses got paid. Let the people who use the water have the say.
Water is too important to leave to shareholders. Put it in public hands and stop the profit-taking.
Keep it running as it is, but make the bosses pay for what they broke. Don't add a new owner to the mess.
Public ownership is the only thing that has worked for me. Rivers and pipes come before profit.
Lenders took the risk, so lenders should take the loss. Local people running it makes sense to me.
Fine the bosses and keep the owners on the hook. Changing who owns it sounds like a long, costly job.
Just get the court to deal with it. The bills are my worry, and I don't trust either side of the argument.
The company has been ripping us off for years. Give the customers a vote and make the lenders wear it.
I rent, and my bills keep going up. Public ownership would stop the dividends being paid out.
Users and workers in charge, with the creditors taking the loss. That's the fairest answer on the table.
